anak-krakatau-20260905.happened: 6 to 8 Sep 2026: ash from Anak Krakatau closed Jakarta's main airport and seven others, affecting about 2,961 flights and 341,000 people.
anak-krakatau-20260905.disagreed: From 5 Sep 02:00 UTC the observatory's only aviation notice said "Ash-cloud is not observed". Before the next one, three days later, Darwin issued 28 advisories, 24 with ash up to fifty thousand feet.
anak-krakatau-20260905.sources: Transport ministry figures via ABC (rows 1-2); PVMBG VONA 2026KRA026 (row 3); Darwin VAAC advisory counts (row 42).

semeru-20260923.happened: In the 30 days to 9 Oct 2026, 28 of Semeru's 92 observatory ash reports pointed where the official area did not reach 10 km from the vent.
semeru-20260923.disagreed: On 23–27 Sep every SIGMET moved the ash south-east while 20 observatory notices said north or north-east. They disagreed; TEPHRA covered both.
semeru-20260923.sources: TEPHRA's own 30-day census (row 4); SIGMET and VONA texts (row 6).

java-live-20261010.happened: Live public feeds over Java and Bali on 10 Oct 2026, 13:00 WIB, recorded for 90 minutes.
